correctness.rationale: Any cycle in a query support admits a nonextendible cyclic orientation; on a query forest, every directed cycle in the comparability quotient (including loops) admits a nonextendible labeling by orienting unique paths in successive components. Conversely, an acyclic quotient ensures every forest orientation can be topologically sorted with the poset. A longest chain hits different shattered components, giving at most \(n-h\) edges; longest-chain-ending ranks provide h independent fibers attaining equality. At equality the longest chain orders all h components uniquely, and Cayley tree counts yield the stated nonoverlapping summation. The accompanying standard-library verifier compared literal label realizability and the theorem for 4,332,544 supports across all 4,231 labeled five-point posets; no infinite conclusion depends on the finite test.

value.rationale: The arbitrary-poset classification identifies an invariant of a natural finite relational learning class, unifies height with coordinate shattering, and gives a graph-theoretic obstruction for every possible query support. Characterizing all maximum supports by uniquely ordered antichain layers and enumerating them by the Cayley-weighted strict-rank-map sum provides new structural/enumerative information beyond the antichain case or routine height counting.
